problem: Find the equation of the tangent hyperplane to the hypersurface $w=z\sqrt{y}-x$ at the point $(-1,4,1,3).$
worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the hypersurface $w=f(x,y,z)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0},{w}_{0})$ on the hypersurface can be written as

$$
w-{w}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(z-{z}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂z}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z\sqrt{y}-x)=-1 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(z\sqrt{y}-x)=\frac{z}{2\sqrt{y}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(z\sqrt{y}-x)=\sqrt{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y,z)=(-1,4,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(-1,4,1) & =-1 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(-1,4,1) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}}=\frac{1}{4} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z}(-1,4,1) & =\sqrt{4}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent hyperplane:

$$
\begin{aligned}w-3 & =(x-(-1))\frac{∂f}{∂x}(-1,4,1)+(y-4)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(-1,4,1)+(z-1)\frac{∂f}{∂z}(-1,4,1) \\ w-3 & =-(x+1)+\frac{1}{4}(y-4)+2(z-1) \\ w-3 & =-x+\frac{1}{4}y+2z-4 \\ x-\frac{1}{4}y-2z+w+1 & =0 \\ 4x-y-8z+4w+4 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
